hints: The probability of a head is p = 0.4, and a tail is q = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6.
Obtaining the first head on the 5th throw means 4 tails followed by a head.
walkthrough: Identify success and failure probabilities: $p = 0.4, \; q = 0.6$.

Apply the geometric distribution formula for $X = 5$:
$$\mathrm{P}(X = 5) = q^4 p = (0.6)^4 (0.4) = 0.1296 \times 0.4 = 0.05184 \approx 0.0518\text{ (3 s.f.)}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Understand the geometric model:
Let $X$ be the number of throws until the first head appears.
$$X \sim \operatorname{Geo}(0.4)$$
Success probability $p = 0.4$, failure probability $q = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$.

Step 2: Apply the probability mass function:
$$\mathrm{P}(X = r) = q^{r-1} p$$
For $r = 5$:
$$\mathrm{P}(X = 5) = (0.6)^4 \times 0.4 = 0.1296 \times 0.4 = 0.05184$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $0.0518$.

hints: The first head is obtained after the 6th throw if and only if the first 6 throws are all tails.
Use the geometric tail probability formula: P(X > k) = q^k, where q = 0.6 and k = 6.
walkthrough:
Express the event $X > 6$ as obtaining 6 consecutive failures (tails):
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 6) = q^6 = (0.6)^6 = 0.046656 \approx 0.0467\text{ (3 s.f.)}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Interpret the inequality:
The first head is obtained after the 6th throw, which means $X > 6$.
This occurs if and only if throws 1 through 6 all result in tails.

Step 2: Apply the geometric tail formula:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > k) = q^k$$
For $k = 6$ with $q = 0.6$:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 6) = (0.6)^6 = 0.046656$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $0.0467$.
